citations.review_text:
You control a reanimated corpse trying to escape an island prison.  It's a side-scrolling platformer.

Multiple different enemies which you can attack using melee (swords, kicks and punches), you also have longer range attacks (bows, grenades, etc.)

Graphics look great, nice and clear with some detailed backgrounds.  Music and sound effects also compliment the game well.  It really shines with player movement, that is precise and smooth, it needs to be as it's fast-paced gameplay.  The controls are easy to use and easy to learn.  A controller is recommended, but I'm playing perfectly fine with mouse and keyboard.

A very enjoyable and difficult game, the devs have accounted for this, if you find it too difficult you can use something called assist mode to make things a little easier.

A fun game to play! :D

I'd forgotten why I had stopped playing this game after briefly obsessing with it on Playstation.

It just isn't what I enjoy out of Metroidvania or roguelikes. I may try out the accessibility settings, but overall if you're anything like me (which is incredibly vague), maybe look for a different Metroidvania or roguelike.

These guys have some serious skill though, and I hope Castlevania turns out good!

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the detailed pixel art and backgrounds.

citations.review_text: Don't let my current playtime fool you, I've played this game over and over and over, to hell and back, leading me to rack up about 500 hours of playtime all together. I am a huge roguelite guy, I've played tons of them, and besides *maybe (and that's a somewhat significant maybe) Risk of Rain 2, I personally think this is the genre's peak--and I consider it to be one of my top 5 favorite games of all time. The artwork (the backgrounds in particular I'd consider to be some of the best pixel art I've ever seen), The music (thematically fitting bangers from front to back), the writing (often funny, yet also sometimes poignant), the clever mechanics and perfect difficulty-modifier system, THE NIGH-UNMATCHED MOMENT TO MOMENT GAMEPLAY (only the other games in my top five (Pizza Tower, Ultrakill, and both Hollow Knights) have gameplay even close to the same level of impactful and satisfying, imo), the insane amount of references, that while I think can interfere with the game's tone a little bit, also show an immense love for video games as an artform, and more go to show that this game, in terms of both being a roguelite (yes, lite, not like) and metroidvania, is a masterpiece... imo :). Besides the tone thing I mentioned before, the fact that the game doesn't really explain to you that you should go all in on one color of scrolls rather that spreading them out, and that we didn't really get a proper ending to the game's story with a final big update (thanks a lot, Motion Twin), I don't really have any truly note-worthy issues with this game. Again, besides RoR2, I don't think there's a single action roguelite that even comes close to the greatness of Dead Cells.

[h1] Not a bad game, by any means. It was simply not my thing and I felt like I could use my money better if put elsewhere. [/h1]

I was bored by it. You can only carry two items, two abilities (think spells), and one consumable (Healing). For those who find the fun in roguelites and roguelikes to be miscellaneous and chaotic stacking of abilities and items, It is underwhelming. If that is you, do not buy this game. 

Additionally, there is little in the way of story or lore. You play to play. There is no grander goal. This is not bad, but just not my thing. If you find that you cannot interact with a game without a story to explore, then do not buy this game.

Deaths are very punishing. The only thing that carries over between runs is some upgrades, and some gold. The enemies were alright, but I was bored by them. Though I never tried any of the bosses, so take this point with a fistful of salt. If punishing gameplay is your thing, then buy this game.

If you like completing games, then this game is up your alley. There are a staggering amount of skins, weapons, maps, and bosses. There are also a lot of upgrades that have carryover between runs that you can get and I can see someone liking the completist aspect of it all.

If you like beautiful-looking games, then this is definitely up there. Best pixel art I have ever seen by a long shot.

One day, when I have mostly gone through my Wishlist, I will give it another shot. Until then, I stand by not really recommending it.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as fast-paced and addictive, featuring smooth movement and responsive combat.

citations.review_text:
9/10

Man, this game just feels GOOD.

Every hit has weight behind it. You smack something and actually feel that sh*t connect. The combat is fast, crunchy and ridiculously satisfying, and there's enough variety that I'm constantly going "alright, one more run" and then somehow another hour dissapears.

What I really like is that it doesn't feel like I've seen everything after a few hours. I'm still finding new stuff, trying different builds, getting my ass kicked, figuring sh*t out and realizing there's a ton I haven't even touched yet. Thats exactly what I want from a game like this.

Not giving it a 10/10 yet, mostly because I still have way too much left to see, and I wanna know if it can keep this feeling going deeper into the game.

But right now? Easy 9/10.

If you're into fast combat, experimenting with builds and that "just ONE more run" addiction... yeah, this sh*t is dangerous.
Between weapon and item variety and fluidity of combat and traversing the levels, Dead Cells is a must play for any roguelike fans, especially if you enjoy fast paced, satisfying combat.

Dead Cells is one of the best roguelike action games I've played. The combat is fast, responsive, and incredibly satisfying, with a huge variety of weapons, skills, and mutations that let you create all kinds of powerful and fun builds. Every run feels different as you experiment with new combinations.

The game features multiple biomes, each with unique enemies, secrets, and branching paths. Choosing which route to take is an important part of every run, as different biomes offer different rewards and levels of difficulty. Exploring hidden rooms and discovering permanent upgrades makes each run feel rewarding, even when you die.

The game can be brutally difficult, but every death feels like a chance to learn and improve rather than a punishment. The smooth controls, satisfying progression, and constant unlocks make it hard to put down.

If you enjoy challenging roguelike action with excellent combat and tons of replayability, Dead Cells is an easy recommendation.

9/10

citations.review_text: Absolutely a great game. The soundtrack is a cherry on top. Anyone who's a roguelike enjoyer should 100% try this game. Plays amazingly on a controller, much better than on a keyboard!

this game is pure skill issue simulator and I love it
I die.
I die again.
I die to a bat.
I die to a door.
I die to my own grenade.
and yet I keep coming back like a clown with a death wish.
the best part?
you can play as a girl.
as a trans person that ♥♥♥♥ made me so happy I almost cried in the Prisoners’ Quarters.
representation in a game where everything wants to murder you? peak.
the combat is buttery.
the builds are broken.
the bosses are trauma.
the soundtrack goes hard while I’m getting folded by a green slime for the 40th time.
I tell myself “one more run” and suddenly it’s 4am and I’m screaming at a timed door.
Dead Cells didn’t just take my free time.
it took my sanity, my sleep schedule, and somehow still made me feel seen.


10/10 would get one-shot again.

Combined with ~150h on my Switch, I can easily say this will forever be one of the best roguelikes around, and it's easily a must play for anyone interested in the genre. The visuals are beautiful, the OST is incredibly underrated, the enemy and weapon variety are fantastic, the combat is brilliant, and it has a surprisingly great sense of humour.

citations.review_text: Higher boss cells get difficult. Good item and build variety. Very replayable.

English Version (french below) : 

The game is super cool but it is SO HARD. On the first few difficulties, it's hard but it's still manageable, after the 3rd boss cell however, it just becomes total madness. 

The gameplay is nice, but it kind of feels... weird to me sometimes. It doesn't feel very precise, jumps are a little weird, hits don't feel as heavy as they should in my opinion, and builds revolve a bit too much about getting the right modifiers on weapons rather than on the weapons themselves, (well it does in the sens that some weapons are just downright unusable I guess). 

The game is really cool though, don't get me wrong, and I especially love the Castlevania DLC (looking forward to their next Castlevania game), there's just quite a lot I didn't really like in the flow of the game.
But apart from that, it has TONS of references and easter eggs to other indie games, the beheaded (protagonist) is overall pretty fun and the gameplay still does feel satisfying once you get used to it.

Overall, I really recommend the game but I don't recommend trying the higher difficulties as I think that's truly when I found problems with the gameplay, in addition to very overtuned enemies and little to no healing (but in a sense, that is sort of a skill issue on my end lol)

Alors attention hein, le jeu est très cool, j'ad…

What can I say about this game that is not already been said in a variety of different ways? It is a fantastic rogue lite with RPG elements, a thoroughly enjoyable combat and skill mechanic that allows for incredible variety in each playthrough, and advanced customization options to really ensure you get the most out of your runs once you understand the game and the fundamentals. It is terrific, and the specific formula has not been replicated by any other game in the genre, and believe me I've tried so many. The graphics are great, the music is great, and the later levels once you have acquired some boss cells take me right back to playing bullet hells from Nintendo in the early 1990s. In the best possible way. The game punishes button mashing in the truest sense and rewards muscle memory, and each tier of biome demands more and more out of the player. It is addictive, but it is also easy to run out of dopamine or see that translated into rage when trying to nominally complete the game. The higher levels are just absurdly punishing. I find that for some reason Steam does not accurately track the unbelievable amount of time I had to sink to beat the fourth BC run, and by contrast the fifth BC was almost easier. I've been playing this game for years. Regardless, like most adventures that have a skill ceiling, it is easy to lose the overarching plot or discover that the end is less climactic than you thought. This is not Hollow Knight, so don't go in expecting some revolutionary amount of lore. In that way, the game is exactly what it says on the label--this is one of the most polished roguelike experiences of this generation. So please play it because you're missing out on a ton of fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes built-in accessibility options that can be used to make the game easier and reach content they otherwise could not access.

citations.review_text: I've loved this game since early access, but it always felt like I'd never be good enough to actually see a large portion of the game. Do yourself a favor, turn on whatever accessibility options keep the game fun to play. After years of playing and never making it to much of the DLC content, I sucked it up, turned on some of the options to make it easier, and am finally seeing some of the content I could never make it to before. I beat Blasphemous without aid, I don't mind learning patterns through repetition, But spending most of an hour just to get back to a boss if I'm lucky would always get old and after a couple tried I'd be done for while. Recently I've played with the ability to continue, and suddenly I don't feel like time spent playing the game is entirely wasted again.

This game is great. 

It's a sort of 2d side scroller with fast paced combat that has a lot of variety and re-playability. 

You start off somewhat weak and through every attempt to progress through the maps and every death you slowly gain power to go further the next time.. and the next... and the next after that. 

Death becomes part of the game. You keep earning currency to unlock permanent upgrades, then try again. You can start with random weapons, or use the options to control what is available. As you move through the levels you find new weapons and items so you can swap or upgrade as you go. Each weapon can change how you fight making it very fun. 

The art is great. It's vibrant and you can clearly see it in the trailers. Unlocking all cosmetics, powers, weapons, and hunting achievements when the path through the worlds you can take each time can change makes this game have a lot of hours of potential gameplay. 

This one is worth the money.
W GAME, really fun, pretty hard and SOOOOO many fun and uniqe builds which all can beat the game with enough skill. Buy this game if you like a challange and like the genre.

3 things are certain: death, taxes and Dead Cells. 

I've been playing this game since it came out in 2018. I've even got it for the Switch. There have been periods were I put the game down to play something else with a battlepass that requires my complete and devout attention to, but when that cycle is broken, I come right back to Dead Cells. 

The gameplay here is just solid. When you get in the flow state, the slow state is strong. There is an anxious amount of weapons and items to use in this game, which CAN feel like a bad thing at times, but that's just the game trying to get you to not stick to the same build every single run. It's all about experimentation, finding different items and weapons that work well together, however obscene it may seem.

There are plenty of enviroments and enemies, bosses are fun to fight. 

Overall, a damn near perfect roguelike. Up there with the greats 100%. A must try for any roguelike enjoyers. 

There's no cross-saves like Hades has, which would have been nice, but since the development for this game is pretty much over, wattayagonnado?

You know it's good when I have over 100 hours and there is still more content.

On a serious note though, even without steam sales, $40 for everything including the DLC is an amazing price for a game with this much content. The game is punishing, yet fair and is what I would consider what a perfect rougelite is. The game has so many fun and goofy weapons to try out and a few of them reference other games, so you could play the game with movesets inspired/taken directly from those characters. Also the bosses are amazing and very fun to fight. I'm willing to say that the high points in the game are from the bosses, and are probably my favorite part of playing the game run, after run, after run.
